title: Mechanics and Valuation of Plain Vanilla Interest Rate Swaps
targetAudiencePersona: Corporate Treasurer & Capital Markets Derivatives Trader
prerequisites: Forward rates and OIS zero curve discounting from Chapter 4
Cost of carry forward pricing parity from Chapter 5
Duration-based hedging and balance sheet immunization from Chapter 6
learningOutcomes: Diagram and calculate net cash flows for plain vanilla fixed-for-floating interest rate swaps.
Execute synthetic debt and asset transformations to lock borrowing costs or float investment returns.
Analyze the comparative advantage argument and calculate net arbitrage surplus sharing across counterparties.
Value existing interest rate swaps via forward rates and OIS discounting, and via bond portfolio decomposition.
Differentiate bilateral replacement credit risk from notional risk and explain post-2008 CCP clearing reforms.

sections.title: The Floating Rate Debt Dilemma & Swap Cash Flows
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Introduce plain vanilla interest rate swaps and explain why notional principal is never exchanged.
keyPoints: Two counterparties agree to exchange fixed interest for floating interest.
Net settlement transfers only (Floating - Fixed) * Notional * (Days / 360).
Notional principal ($100M) is purely a scaling factor and never changes hands.
sections.formulaUsed: Net Flow = (R_fl - R_fix) * L * Delta t

sections.title: Synthetic Liability & Asset Transformations
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Show how companies and investors synthetically transform debts and assets using swaps.
keyPoints: Borrowers with floating bank loans (SOFR + 1%) pay fixed 5% in swap, locking fixed rate at 6%.
Investors holding 6% fixed bonds pay fixed 5% and receive SOFR, creating floating return SOFR + 1%.
Eliminates interest rate vulnerability without restructuring underlying loan contracts.

sections.title: Swap Bank Market Makers & Bid-Offer Spreads
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate the role of financial intermediaries and matched swap books.
keyPoints: Swap banks act as market makers quoting bid-ask spreads (e.g., 4.98% bid vs 5.02% ask).
Matched books earn 4 bps ($40,000/yr per $100M) risk-free without directional market exposure.
Banks warehouse residual mismatch risk and hedge using Treasury and Eurodollar futures.

sections.title: The Comparative Advantage Arbitrage Surplus
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Deconstruct Hull Section 7.4 quality spread differentials and surplus sharing.
keyPoints: Firm A (AAA) borrows fixed 10.0% / floating SOFR+0.3%; Firm B (BBB) borrows fixed 11.2% / floating SOFR+1.0%.
Fixed spread difference is 1.2% (120 bps); floating spread difference is 0.7% (70 bps).
Total arbitrage surplus equals 120 - 70 = 50 bps, shared among Firm A (20 bps), Firm B (20 bps), and Bank (10 bps).
sections.formulaUsed: Total Surplus = Delta Fixed Spread - Delta Floating Spread

sections.title: Valuation via Forward Rates, OIS & CCP Clearing
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate swap valuation via forward rates and bond decomposition, and review CCP risk reforms.
keyPoints: Swap value is zero at inception; revalued as PV of forward floating minus fixed cash flows discounted at OIS.
Decomposed as V_swap = B_fl - B_fix, where floating bond resets to par at coupon dates.
Credit risk is strictly replacement cost max(0, V_swap), safeguarded by mandatory CCP clearing.
sections.formulaUsed: V_swap = sum((F_i - K) * Delta t * P(0, t_i))

misconceptions.misconception: Counterparties in an interest rate swap exchange the $100M principal at inception and maturity.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Notional principal is purely a calculation scale; principal is never exchanged, eliminating 100% of notional principal default risk.

misconceptions.misconception: Entering an interest rate swap requires paying an upfront fee or purchase price.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: The contractual fixed swap rate is set at the par swap rate, ensuring initial net present value is exactly zero.

misconceptions.misconception: If a swap counterparty defaults, the entire $100M notional principal is lost.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Counterparty risk is strictly bilateral replacement cost max(0, V_swap), and modern CCP clearing enforces daily mark-to-market variation margin.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: Firm A (AAA rated) can borrow fixed at 10.0% or floating at SOFR + 0.3%. Firm B (BBB rated) can borrow fixed at 11.2% or floating at SOFR + 1.0%. A financial intermediary arranges an interest rate swap.
activeRecallQuiz.question: What is the total comparative advantage arbitrage surplus available to be shared between the counterparties and the bank?
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Total surplus equals (Fixed Spread Difference) minus (Floating Spread Difference) = (11.2% - 10.0%) - (1.0% - 0.3%) = 1.2% - 0.7% = 0.50% (50 basis points).

coreTakeaways: Plain vanilla swaps exchange fixed for floating payments; notional principal is never exchanged.
Combining floating bank debt with a fixed-payer swap synthetically locks fixed borrowing rates.
Swap market makers earn bid-ask spreads on matched books without taking directional interest rate risk.
Comparative advantage arises from quality spread differentials, creating arbitrage surplus for all parties.
Swaps have zero value at inception and are valued via forward rate modeling and OIS zero discounting.
Credit risk in interest rate swaps represents bilateral replacement cost, fully mitigated by CCP clearing.
